cards.title: 2.1 Climate and Meteorological Instrumentation
body: 2.1 Climate and Meteorological Instrumentation

**Climate** is defined as **the general state of the atmosphere over a long period of time, resulting from energy and mass exchange within the atmosphere and between the atmosphere and the Earth's surface.** Unlike weather, which describes short-term atmospheric changes, climate determines an area's long-term suitability for crop and livestock production. The major elements of climate that affect agricultural productivity include rainfall, temperature, relative humidity, solar radiation, light, wind, and topography.

To plan farming activities, agricultural scientists and farmers rely on weather data collected consistently on a daily basis (typically before 8:00 a.m.) at meteorological stations. Specialized instruments are used to measure different atmospheric elements:
*   **Standard Rain Gauge** and **Mechanical Rainfall Recorder**:

cards.title: Natural Resource Base
body:
| Meteorological Instrument | Climate Element Measured | Standard Unit of Measurement | Practical Agricultural Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Standard Rain Gauge** | Precipitation (Rainfall) | Millimeters ($$\text{mm}$$) | Determines crop planting dates and water availability |
| **Digital Thermometer** | Temperature | Degrees Celsius ($$^\circ\text{C}$$) | Identifies frost risks and crop growth thresholds |
| **Thermo-hygrograph** | Temperature & Relative Humidity | $^\circ\text{C}$$ and Percentage ($$\%$$) | Predicts disease outbreaks (e.g., downy mildew) |
| **Anemometer** | Wind Speed | Meters per second ($$\text{m/s}$$) or Knots | Evaluates soil erosion risk and crop lodging hazards |
| **Evaporation Pan** | Evaporation Rate | Millimeters ($$\text{mm}$$) | Calculates irrigation water requirements |

cards.title: 2.2 Soil Formation, Profiles, and Physical Properties
body: 2.2 Soil Formation, Profiles, and Physical Properties

**Soil** is defined as **a loose earth material derived from parent materials (rocks) through physical, chemical, and biological weathering processes.** It serves as a natural habitat for plants and soil organisms, and is an indispensable resource for human livelihood. Soil science is divided into two primary approaches:
*   **Pedology**: The study of soil origin (genesis), classification, mapping, and physical/chemical description.
*   **Edaphology**: The study of soil properties in relation to plant growth and crop production.

Soil formation is an extremely slow process; it takes approximately $$120\text{ to }400\text{ years}$$ to form just $$1\text{ cm}$$ of soil, meaning a standard $$20\text{ cm}$$ topsoil layer requires $$2\,400\text{ to }8\,000\text{ years}$$ to develop. The five major factors controlling soil formation

cards.title: Natural Resource Base
body:
| Soil Horizon | Common Name | Primary Composition | Key Ecological Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **O-Horizon** | Organic Layer | Decomposing organic matter, leaf litter | Feeds soil organisms; insulates soil surface |
| **A-Horizon** | Topsoil | Mineral particles mixed with dark humus | Primary zone for seed germination and nutrient uptake |
| **B-Horizon** | Subsoil | Accumulated clays, iron, and aluminum | Stores water and deep nutrients; supports tree roots |
| **C-Horizon** | Parent Material | Unconsolidated weathered rock fragments | Represents the chemical foundation for soil development |

> **💡 Did You Know?**: The upper portion of the regolith (comprising the O, A, and B horizons) is called the **solum**. The solum represents the true, biochemically active soil layer capable of fully supporting plant root systems.

cards.problem: Which meteorological instrument is used to continuously and simultaneously record both ambient temperature and relative humidity?

steps.text: A thermo-hygrograph is a specialized meteorological instrument designed to record both temperature (thermo) and relative humidity (hygro) continuously and simultaneously on a single rotating chart.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: What is the average volume composition of mineral solids in a loam surface soil under ideal conditions for crop growth?

steps.text: According to the standard soil volume composition documented in Figure 2.4, an ideal loam surface soil contains $$45\%$$ mineral solids, $$5\%$$ organic matter, and approximately $$25\%$$ air and $$25\%$$ water.
Thus, the volume share of mineral solids is **$$45\%$$**.

cards.problem: A salt-affected soil characterized by an electrical conductivity ($$EC_{se}$$) greater than $$4\text{ dS/m}$$, an exchangeable sodium percentage (ESP) less than $$15\%$$, and a pH less than $$8.5$$ is classified as:

steps.text: According to Table 2.6, a saline soil has high soluble salts ($$EC_{se} > 4\text{ dS/m}$$), but low exchangeable sodium ($$ESP < 15\%$$\) and a moderate pH ($$pH < 8.5$$\). Sodic and saline-sodic soils have an ESP greater than $$15\%$$.

Weathering breaks rocks down into **regolith** (unconsolidated material overlying bedrock). Rocks are grouped into three classes:
*   **Igneous**: Formed from molten magma (e.g., granite, diorite, gabbro, and basalt).
*   **Sedimentary**: Formed from the deposition and re-cementation of weathered materials (e.g., sandstone, shale, limestone, and dolomite).
*   **Metamorphic**: Formed when igneous or sedimentary rocks are altered by extreme heat and pressure (e.g., gneiss, schist, quartzite, slate, and marble).

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: The scientific study of soil properties specifically in relation to plant growth and crop production is called:

steps.text: While pedology is the study of soil origin, classification, and description, edaphology is the study of soil properties in relation to plant growth, crop production, and agricultural management.
Thus, this branch of soil science is **Edaphology**.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: Which soil textural class has particle diameters strictly less than $$0.002\text{ mm}$$, forming the highly active soil colloids?

steps.text: According to physical soil separate sizes (Table 2.4), clay particles have a diameter of less than $$0.002\text{ mm}$$. Due to this extremely small size, they possess a large surface area and act as chemically active soil colloids.
Therefore, the correct textural class is **Clay**.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: What is the recommended chemical amendment used to reclaim sodic soils by supplying Calcium ($$Ca^{2+}$$) to displace exchangeable Sodium ($$Na^+$$)?

steps.text: Gypsum ($$CaSO_4$$) is highly effective for sodic soil reclamation (Table 2.7). It dissolves to supply $$Ca^{2+}$$ ions, which replace the exchangeable $$Na^+$$ on clay colloid surfaces. The displaced $$Na^+$$ is then washed out as soluble $$Na_2SO_4$$.

cards.title: Natural Resource Base
body: In mountainous or hilly terrains, **topography** plays a major role in shaping local climates. Topographical factors like elevation (altitude), slope steepness, and aspect (direction of the slope) affect temperature, wind velocity, and rainfall patterns. For example, soils on steep slopes are highly prone to water erosion, whereas valley soils are deeper, richer, and more suitable for crop cultivation due to the deposition of eroded materials.

cards.title: Natural Resource Base
body:
A vertical cross-section of the soil reveals distinct horizontal layers called **soil horizons**. Together, these horizons make up the **soil profile**:
*   **O-Horizon**: Organic layer at the surface, composed of leaf litter and decaying matter.
*   **A-Horizon**: Mineral layer at or near the surface, rich in dark, humified organic matter.
*   **B-Horizon**: Subsurface mineral layer where silicate clays, iron, or aluminum accumulate through **illuviation** (washing-in).
*   **C-Horizon**: Unconsolidated parent material, little affected by soil-forming processes, retaining original rock structures.

cards.title: 2.3 Soil Composition and Physics Calculations
body: 2.3 Soil Composition and Physics Calculations

Soil is a three-phase system composed of solids, liquids, and gases. An ideal loam surface soil under optimal conditions for plant growth is composed of approximately:
*   **$$45\%$$ Mineral Solids**: Inorganic particles of sand, silt, and clay.
*   **$$5\%$$ Organic Matter**: Decaying plant and animal residues and stable humus.
*   **$$20\%\text{ to }30\%$$ Air**: Occupies open pore spaces when the soil is dry.
*   **$$20\%\text{ to }30\%$$ Water**: Occupies pore spaces and forms the **soil solution** containing dissolved plant nutrients.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: Under standard soil profile classification, which horizon is known as the zone of accumulation or illuviation of clays and oxides?

steps.text: The B-horizon (subsoil) is characterized as the zone of accumulation (illuviation), where fine silicate clays, iron, aluminum, or organic matter washed down from the overlying A-horizon accumulate.
Therefore, the zone of accumulation is the **B-horizon**.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: Which of the following cations is known to cause clay dispersion, breaking down soil aggregates and causing soil-crusting?

steps.text: Sodium ($$Na^+$$) ions have a large hydrated radius and single charge. When dominant, they cause clay particles to disperse (separate), which destroys soil structure. Calcium, magnesium, and aluminum promote flocculation (aggregation).
